brief.industry_meta: Data & AI Platform · Lakehouse / Enterprise AI
brief.deck: Databricks closed $5B at a $190B valuation on 13 August, 42% above its $134B Series L mark six months earlier, on a revenue run-rate past $7B growing more than 80% a year. Enterprise data brands hold a seat at almost every Formula 1 team.
brief.the_case_p1: Databricks announced on 13 August that it had closed a $5B strategic round at a $190B valuation, led by Coatue, with Blackstone, MGX and T. Rowe Price accounts, and new money from Sixth Street Growth, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG. Its own release puts the revenue run-rate past $7B at more than 80% growth. The mark is 42% above the $134B Series L of six months earlier. Ali Ghodsi has said publicly that this is a poor year to list, so the money is the balance sheet, not a roadshow.
brief.the_case_p2: Enterprise data brands already treat motorsport as a proven channel, and the Formula 1 grid is close to sold: Oracle at Oracle Red Bull Racing, SAP at Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team, Splunk at McLaren F1 Team, IBM at Scuderia Ferrari, VAST at Atlassian Williams Racing, CoreWeave at Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team. On the Formula E grid, six of the ten entries carry no data, AI or software partner at all.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 13 August, and brand budgets are written in the quarter after one. Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters this autumn, and the GEN4 era opens at the Jeddah E-Prix in December - the largest technical reset the championship has had.
brief.why_team_para: Nissan's rows in the sponsor table are the parent, Alpine Tech on the powertrain and legacy entries still marked unverified - nothing in the technology category, and the team profile lists enterprise software as open. It is the works entry of the manufacturer now supplying the GEN4 powertrain to Andretti as well, so one platform reaches two garages. Rowland's Season 11 title is the shop window.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO NISSAN FORMULA E TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Formula E is an energy-management contest: a fixed allocation, attack mode, regeneration and the slipstream, won by whoever models it best. A lakehouse unifying telemetry, energy, tyre and timing data, with models run between sessions, is that lever, and no testing cap limits the software. Nissan's GEN4 powertrain also runs at Andretti, so one platform serves two data sets.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Data and AI Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, covering the GEN4 cycle. Estimated $3-6M a year, part-payable in platform credits. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming of the team's data environment, and a joint programme with Nissan's own data organisation.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Schultz has run Databricks' marketing since March 2017, after leading marketing at Alteryx through its listing; brand and sponsorship sit with him. Path: Ali Ghodsi, co-founder and chief executive since 2016, and Ion Stoica, co-founder and executive chair.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Rick, Oracle, SAP, Splunk, IBM and VAST have each bought a Formula 1 team. Six of the ten Formula E entries have no data partner at all, and Nissan holds a drivers' title. 25 minutes before the rosters close?”
score_cells: $5B closed 13 Aug; Season 13 rosters close this autumn.
Proven category in motorsport, but Formula E is the smaller stage.
No listing to time against; the GEN4 reset is the only clock.
MODE A: energy modelling is the team's competitive lever.
risks: FORMULA E IS THE SMALLER STAGE
A company valued at $190B can afford Formula 1, which delivers several times the audience. A Formula E recommendation will be challenged internally on reach alone.
The Formula 1 data lane is bought at every team a brand this size would want. Formula E buys the category outright, with a workstream that is real rather than decorative.
Google Cloud is Formula E's cloud and technology partner. Databricks runs on the hyperscalers rather than against them, but the championship may read the categories as neighbouring.
Scope the designation as data and AI at team level and clear it before signature. McLaren carries Splunk and Google Cloud on the same car.
brief.bottom_line: A $5B round closed at $190B on 13 August, a revenue run-rate past $7B growing more than 80% a year, and no listing to wait for. The Formula 1 data lane is bought at every team a brand this size would want, six of the ten Formula E entries carry no data partner, and the works team that holds a drivers' title has an open enterprise-software lane.

why_now.label: The business under the round

These are the company's own figures from its own release, not audited accounts, and the brief attributes them that way.

why_now.label: A re-pricing, not a listing

Ali Ghodsi said in June 2026 that this is a poor year to go public, and no public or confidential S-1 had been filed as of mid-August, with a listing widely expected in 2027 or later. That matters commercially: there is no quiet period and no roadshow, so a multi-year brand commitment can be signed now rather than deferred.

why_now.label: The calendar
why_now.text: Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters through the autumn. Season 13 is the first season of the GEN4 regulations - the championship's largest technical reset - opening at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and running 21 races across 13 cities, with the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027, the Miami E-Prix two weeks later and the Tokyo E-Prix closing on 24-25 July 2027.

why_team.label: The Formula 1 lane is bought; the Formula E lane is not
why_team.text: On the Formula 1 grid the data, cloud and enterprise-software categories are occupied almost everywhere: Oracle at Red Bull, SAP and Microsoft and Hewlett Packard Enterprise at Mercedes, Splunk and Dell and Google Cloud at McLaren, HP and IBM at Ferrari, Atlassian and VAST at Williams, CoreWeave at Aston Martin, Microsoft at Alpine, TWG AI and Core Scientific at Cadillac, with AWS and Salesforce at championship level. On the Formula E grid only Andretti, Envision, Mahindra and Jaguar carry a data or AI partner. Six of the ten entries carry none.

why_team.label: Nissan's lane is open on the table, not by assertion
why_team.text: The sponsor table records no data, AI or software partner at Nissan Formula E Team. Alpine Tech is the renewed partner that helped develop the Nissan e-4ORCE 05 powertrain, and the remaining rows - Coral, Crowe, Nagase, Castrol - are legacy entries the table still marks unverified. The team profile lists enterprise software and EV tech as open categories. Official Data and AI Partner would be a first there.

why_team.label: One partnership, two garages
why_team.text: Nissan announced a multi-year agreement to supply its GEN4 Formula E powertrain to Andretti Formula E from Season 13. A data platform bought at the works team therefore sits at the centre of a powertrain relationship spanning two entries, which is more telemetry, more validation and more of the story that makes an enterprise reference customer credible.

why_team.label: A works team with something to show
why_team.text: Oliver Rowland won the Season 11 drivers' world championship for Nissan and stays for a fourth campaign under a multi-year agreement, with Zane Maloney alongside for Season 13. Beyond the garage, the partnership opens a route into Nissan's own enterprise data estate - manufacturing, connected vehicles, supply chain - which is where a motorsport deal earns back more than it costs for a company selling what Databricks sells.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Formula E is decided by energy management: a fixed allocation per race, attack mode, regeneration and the slipstream, resolved by whoever models consumption and rivals' strategies best. A lakehouse unifying telemetry, energy, tyre, weather and timing data, with machine-learning models run between sessions and on the pit wall, is that lever. Unlike Formula 1 there is no aerodynamic-testing restriction shaping where a team may spend its effort, so the software lever is comparatively larger.

value.label: The GEN4 reset makes it worth more
value.text: Season 13 is the first season of GEN4. Every energy model, tyre model and strategy assumption a team holds is rebuilt from a smaller base of data. A partner that arrives at the start of that cycle is embedded in how the team learns the new car, which is a far stronger position than joining a settled formula, and it is why the timing rather than the money is the argument.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner selling to chief data officers and chief information officers brings a guest list of enterprise buyers to the Austin, Miami and Tokyo rounds, and a co-produced engineering content strand that gives the team technical credibility rather than another logo. For a works team whose commercial roster is thin outside the manufacturer, a category-defining technology partner is a signal to the rest of the market.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Data and AI Partner designation, sidepod and halo placement, naming of the team's data environment, engineer and driver access for Databricks' channels, hospitality at the US and Tokyo rounds, and a joint programme with Nissan's own data organisation - the part of the deal that makes it defensible to a chief financial officer.

ruled_out.reason: Oracle is title partner and the incumbent data and cloud brand.
SAP, Microsoft and Hewlett Packard Enterprise all sit on the roster.
Splunk, Dell Technologies and Google Cloud occupy analytics, hardware and cloud.
HP is title partner and IBM holds the enterprise software and cloud lane.
Atlassian as title partner and VAST on the data platform - the closest direct clash on the grid.

ruled_out.team: Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team · BWT Alpine F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: CoreWeave holds AI cloud at Aston Martin; Microsoft holds cloud at Alpine.
TWG AI and Core Scientific occupy the AI and compute lanes on the first roster.
TWG AI is primary partner and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner - and Andretti is a Nissan powertrain customer, so the works team reaches it anyway.

ruled_out.team: Envision Racing · Mahindra Racing · Jaguar TCS Racing
ruled_out.reason: Sand Technologies, Tech Mahindra and TCS respectively already hold the data and technology lane at each.
TDK holds the official technology designation; title rights are open but priced as title rights.

ruled_out.team: DS Penske · Cupra Kiro · Citroën Racing · Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
ruled_out.reason: Open on data, but none offers the works-team engineering programme or the two-garage powertrain reach that makes the workstream real.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Rick Schultz before Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters, to size an Official Data and AI Partner entry at Nissan Formula E Team across the GEN4 cycle, agree how the designation is scoped against the championship's own cloud partner, and put an energy-modelling proof of concept in front of the team's race engineers.

# Databricks → Nissan Formula E Team — verification log (N° 235, 13 Aug 2026)

An n8n-engine row (27 Aug 2026, score 87, "HOT TOP TIER", person Ali Ghodsi) rebuilt as a full case
at no model-API cost. n8n surfaced Databricks four times — 7 May at 84, 4 Jun at 76, 27 Jul at 89,
27 Aug at 87 — without ever pinning a trigger. Nothing it recorded was carried over.

global.nissannews.com and allied.vc were blocked by the egress proxy. Every claim below was checked

## Why Formula E, on the evidence rather than on preference

The Formula 1 answer was tested first and it fails on occupancy. Every Formula 1 team a brand at
this valuation would want already carries a data, cloud or enterprise-software partner — the table
rows are in the ledger above — so entering Formula 1 means displacing an incumbent, taking a
second-tier designation beside one, or buying a team without an engineering story. The two Formula 1
rosters with room are the ones a $190B company would not choose for reach.

Formula E is the opposite: six of ten entries carry no data partner at all, and the operational case
is genuinely stronger there. Formula E is an energy-management formula — fixed energy per race,
attack mode, regeneration, slipstream — decided by modelling rather than by aerodynamic development,
and it has no aerodynamic-testing restriction shaping where a team may spend effort. Season 13 is the
first GEN4 season, so every energy and tyre model is rebuilt from a small base of data. That is a
real Mode A workstream, not a halo.

## Honest score — what holds it back (81, not the 87 n8n recorded)

- **Brand fit 15/20.** The category is proven in motorsport, but Formula E's reach is a fraction of
  Formula 1's for a company that could pay Formula 1 prices. This is the first objection the brief
  will meet internally and it is the first risk row on page 2.
- **Urgency 13/20.** There is no listing to time against. Ghodsi has deferred it, which removes the
  quiet-period pressure that usually drives this desk's HOT TOP TIER scores. The GEN4 reset is a
  window, not a deadline.
- **Capacity 19/20, not 20.** The money is unquestionable; the constraint is that a works-OEM entry
  means the partner sits behind the Nissan marque rather than beside it.
- **On-camera 3/4.** A works Formula E car is a manufacturer's canvas first.

## Leadership ties

`leadership_ties`: **none found**. Ali Ghodsi, Ion Stoica, Rick Schultz and Hatim Shafique show no
Formula 1 or Formula E role in any listing checked, and no prior motorsport sponsorship structured by
any of them was found. Schultz's relevant experience is taking a data-analytics brand through a
listing at Alteryx, which is the pattern, not a tie.

## Not claimed

- **No CFO is named.** No Databricks CFO was confirmed in this session, so the decision path stops at
  the executive chair rather than inventing one. The brief says who is listed and no more.
- **No total-funding or ARR figure** beyond the company's own run-rate statement, which is attributed
  as such.
- **Deal size ($3-6M a year) is an ESTIMATE**, labelled as such on the app page.
- **Andy Kofoid** appears in one secondary listing as President, Global Field Operations. A single
  unconfirmed source is not enough for a decision path, so he is not in the brief.
- **Google Cloud is Formula E's championship cloud and technology partner.** Databricks runs on the
  hyperscalers rather than against them, so this is treated as an adjacency to be scoped and cleared,
  named as the second risk row, with the McLaren precedent (Splunk and Google Cloud on one car) as
  the counter — not as a hard clash.
